Czeladz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Czeladź, Poland

Demolished. Czeladź's Jewish community grew significantly from the mid-19th century; by 1921, 753 Jews (4%) were mostly killed at Auschwitz-Birkenau 1942-1943. This cemetery was founded in 1916 as a joint burial site for both Czeladź and neighboring Będzin's Jewish communities, divided into separate sections. Rabbi Cwi Henoch Ha-Kohen Lewin of Będzin was buried here in 1935 beneath a dedicated ohel. During the Holocaust, the cemetery received about 100 victims of a 1939 synagogue burning in Będzin and roughly 400 more from that ghetto's liquidation; burials continued sporadically into 1945 (including victims Marian Grossman and Szlamko Gelbard, killed August 17, 1945), with the last burial - Dawid Siwek - in 1948. Rabbi Lewin's remains were exhumed and reburied in Israel in 1979. In the 1980s, Czeladź-born Moniek Stawski funded fencing and restoration; the site now holds about 3,200 tombstones across 88 male and 91 female rows.
